heroHeadline: Teodoro Calls China Coast Guard Ramming a 'Criminal Act,' Says Manila Developing Options to Deter Further Incidents
heroSubtitle: Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. escalated Manila's characterization of the September 18 China Coast Guard ramming of the BFAR vessel BRP Datu Magat Salamat off Palawan, saying on September 21, 2026 that the incident is 'not merely a violation of maritime rules and regulations, but a criminal act' by the CCG, and confirming the Department of National Defense is 'already developing options for addressing this' with the National Security Adviser and National Maritime Council. Teodoro also condemned Filipinos who publicly defend China's actions in the dispute as committing treason. PCG spokesperson Jay Tarriela described the ramming as the first documented case of a Chinese vessel deliberately striking an unarmed Philippine civilian government ship, and renewed calls for additional Philippine maritime assets. The statement builds on the DFA's formal condemnation of the CCG's 'illegal, coercive, aggressive and dangerous' acts and continued through September 22-23 as the DND consultations proceeded, while China's Foreign Ministry and CCG have not altered their position blaming the Philippine vessel.
